theme_note: These codes share the practice of turning pixel placers into named participants who invite, join, hand work on, or seek visibility. What varies is whether gathering happens by private message, public appeal, flair, a recruiting sign, or an offer of a pixel.
regrouped_from: reviewed across all slices; kept separate from moving coordination beyond Reddit because joining the group and choosing a work venue are different practices

second_order: building, expanding, and patching the spiral
theme_note: These codes put pixels into growth, repair, geometry, or routine maintenance. They vary between expanding outward, correcting rogue pixels, refreshing to avoid duplicate work, and keeping the center or sign sound.
regrouped_from: reviewed across all slices; direct pixel work stayed separate from deciding tasks and boundaries

second_order: setting tasks, roles, and boundaries together
theme_note: These codes make collective choices about priorities, jobs, polls, limits, and what counts as the core. They vary from asking what to do, through voting, to issuing a current task or accepting a limit.
regrouped_from: regrouped from an initial patching-and-expansion group because deciding the rule is a different practice from carrying out pixel work

second_order: making the spiral sacred, funny, and worth remembering
theme_note: These codes praise, pray over, joke about, mourn, or make art from the spiral. The tone ranges from holy-spiral language and optical jokes to loss, pride, and playful invented ailments.
regrouped_from: reviewed across all slices; kept separate from thanking and recounting contributions because these codes work on the spiral's meaning rather than crediting participants

second_order: making and defending the R/SQSP sign
theme_note: These codes treat the sign as a build, a shortened design, disputed labor, a defended object, and a recruiting route. What varies is designing it, deciding its length, maintaining it, and objecting when earlier work is abandoned.
regrouped_from: regrouped from recruiting because the shared practice is making and defending the sign, even when its stated purpose is recruitment

second_order: asking neighbors for peace, borders, and help
theme_note: These codes conduct neighbor-facing diplomacy: proposing truces and borders, receiving offers, asking for aid, negotiating shared designs, and repairing agreements. They vary in who initiates and whether the requested exchange concerns space, protection, help, or altered colors.
regrouped_from: reviewed across all slices; kept separate from judging artwork and from assigning blame because an exchange with a neighbor is the common practice here

second_order: deciding what art to go behind or go over
theme_note: These codes decide whether flags, signs, characters, banners, and the spiral itself deserve room or removal. They vary between granting permission, pleading for protection, refusing new art, and declaring an object expendable.
regrouped_from: regrouped from diplomacy because many passages decide the standing of artwork without negotiating a reciprocal relation

second_order: rallying against the Void and other attacks
theme_note: These codes alert, summon help, focus pixels, refuse surrender, and answer threats. They vary from anticipated attack and border alarms to red-only patching, outside appeals, taunts, and holding until an attack passes.
regrouped_from: reviewed across all slices; kept separate from rebuilding because rallying holds or fights during danger while rebuilding changes what returns afterward

second_order: moving coordination and tools beyond the thread
theme_note: These codes direct coordination to Discord or display an external organizing venue. They vary between welcoming newcomers there, opening the server, and moving crisis defense into it.
regrouped_from: reviewed across all slices; kept separate from recruitment because the defining practice is relocating coordination

theme_note: These codes preserve appeals whose images or removed bodies leave little more than the title. What varies is the urgency and addressee; the shared practice is publicly asking the room while the requested substance is unavailable.
regrouped_from: reviewed across all slices; retained as a small theme because the missing bodies do not justify assigning these appeals to a more specific practice

second_order: separating allies from randos and repairing blame
theme_note: These codes distinguish organized communities and authorized speakers from trolls, randos, mistaken placers, or unofficial claims. They vary between denial, apology, clarification of authority, and disavowing hostility.
regrouped_from: regrouped from neighbor diplomacy because the practice is attribution and repair of blame, not making a new bargain

second_order: shrinking, relocating, and rebuilding the core
theme_note: These codes respond to territorial loss by dropping battles, moving or downsizing the core, preserving coordinates, rebuilding, and explaining recovery. They vary between reluctant retreat, a celebrated rebirth, changed walls, and participant explanations of what the Void made possible.
regrouped_from: regrouped from defending the spiral because survival by changing and rebuilding the design differs from holding it against an immediate attack

second_order: thanking and recounting what spiralers did
theme_note: These codes mark a handoff or ending by crediting work, recalling survival, and thanking participants. They vary between retirement, pride after a crisis, collective farewell, and a compact list of expanding, patching, relocating, and recreating.
regrouped_from: reviewed across all slices; kept separate from commemoration because these passages explicitly account for participants and their work

second_order: carrying the spiral on after Place
theme_note: These codes keep contact, seek cleanup, build on successor canvases, and remake the spiral as physical or digital art after placement ends. What varies is whether continuity takes the form of a venue, a new canvas, a bead image, requested animation, or preservation of battle scars.
regrouped_from: reviewed across all slices; opened in slice 03 because this practice begins after the event closes
